sentences.text: Every entry on a cairn site becomes HTML through one function that the site supplies: the adapter's `rendering.render`.
The edit page's live preview and every public page call that same function, so the preview can't drift from the published page.
The engine ships no public design: its DaisyUI and Tailwind styling covers the admin alone, and the HTML an entry turns into is each site's to decide.
The site builds the function with `createRenderer`, whose pipeline renders plain markdown, tables, `cairn:` links, and `media:` references with no component registered.

The preview calls the function in the editor's browser as the author types, and the public entry route calls it from a SvelteKit server `load`, so the adapter module and everything its `render` imports, components and plugins included, load in the admin's client bundle as well as on the server.

A custom public component is a container directive in the markdown that the site's `build` function turns into markup, and one registry of them is read by both the render pipeline and the editor's component picker.
Two sites start from different places.
On the add-cairn tutorial's site, the adapter at `src/lib/cairn.config.ts` renders over an empty registry, and its developer works through every section.
On a scaffolded site, the adapter at `src/theme/cairn.config.ts` already has the render function, the smartypants plugin, and nine components declared in `markdown-components.ts` under `src/theme/`.
Its developer comes to add a component beside those nine, change an option, or learn what a built-in step emits.
By the end, the site has a render function with its options set, a remark plugin, and a registered custom public component that the preview and the published page render the same way.
Four narrower needs also bring a developer to this page.
A block that has to differ on each use, which a fragment's fixed text can't do, is a component whose attributes each use sets.
An island starts as a component declared with `hydrate`, and its `build` output stays on the page as the static fallback.
Renderer options, such as a wider sanitize allowlist or a different anchor `rel`, are set in [Set the renderer options](#set-the-renderer-options).
For a symptom such as a directive printed as literal text or a code block with no token colors, see [Diagnose a failed check](#diagnose-a-failed-check).
The page assumes you know TypeScript and the unified plugin model, in which a remark plugin works on the markdown tree and a rehype plugin on the HTML tree.
It also assumes you can build a hast element with hastscript's `h()`.
It assumes no cairn knowledge beyond the adapter file.
This page leaves the following topics to the pages that cover them:
What the sanitize floor and the sink guard protect, and what turning the floor off costs, in [Render safety](security-model.md#render-safety).
Hydrating a component in the browser, in [Add an island](add-an-island.md).
Styling the rendered output, in [Style rendered markdown](theme-your-public-site.md#style-rendered-markdown).
Fragments and `::include`, in [Reuse content across entries](reuse-content-across-entries.md).
The media resolver and missing assets, in [Configure media](configure-media.md).
Rendering is set in the adapter file of the site you are changing, and a component builds its markup with `hastscript`.
Before you start, make sure you have the following:
The adapter file, `src/lib/cairn.config.ts` on the tutorial's site or `src/theme/cairn.config.ts` on a scaffolded site.
The tutorial writes its adapter in [Write the site config and a minimal adapter](add-cairn-to-a-sveltekit-app.md#write-the-site-config-and-a-minimal-adapter).
The [hastscript](https://github.com/syntax-tree/hastscript) package, which the following command installs:
A scaffolded site already renders through one `createRenderer` call that carries the smartypants plugin and a registry of the nine components in `markdown-components.ts`.
On that site, skip [Build the render function](#build-the-render-function) and [Add a remark plugin](#add-a-remark-plugin), and add your component to that module's list.
The adapter's `rendering.render` turns an entry's markdown into HTML, and the edit page's preview and every public page call that same function.
Its type is `SiteRender`, which takes one object and resolves to an HTML string with no headings:
To build the render function, follow these steps:
In the adapter file, call `createRenderer` once with the site's registry, and keep the `renderMarkdown` it returns.
The tutorial's site already calls it over `defineRegistry({ components: [] })`, which [Register the component](#register-the-component) replaces.
In the adapter's `rendering` group, set `render` to pass `body` and the three resolvers to `renderMarkdown`.
The preview and the public routes each pass their own resolvers, and `render` forwards every one it receives.
The [`SiteRender`](../reference/core.md#siterender) entry lists which resolver each caller passes.

The `resolveFragment` wiring belongs to [Reuse content across entries](reuse-content-across-entries.md#forward-resolvefragment-from-your-render), and the `resolveMedia` wiring to [Configure media](configure-media.md).
On a scaffolded site, `render` also falls back to the public media resolver when its caller passes none.
`renderMarkdown` fits `SiteRender` because it returns the HTML alone.
A route that needs the headings for a table of contents calls `renderDocument` instead.
It returns the HTML plus the headings in document order, each as `{ id, text, depth }`.
The [`createRenderer`](../reference/core.md#createrenderer) entry shows that return value with an example.
The two callers run `render` at different moments.
The edit page reruns it from an effect debounced on the live body, and it discards a result when a newer render has started.
The public routes call the same `render` in the entry loader, at build when the route is prerendered and per request otherwise.
With the render function in place, look at what the pipeline already does before you add to it.
Before a site adds a component or a plugin, a renderer over an empty registry already highlights code, wraps each table, and places figures.
The highlighter runs on every render and emits class-only output: `cairn-tok-*` classes on spans inside a `pre.shiki` block, with no inline style.
On a public page it runs where the route renders, at build or per request, and the page ships no highlighter to the browser.
The edit page's preview runs `render` in the editor's browser, and the highlighter loads there.
It preloads `js`, `ts`, `jsx`, `tsx`, `svelte`, `html`, `css`, `json`, `bash`, `markdown`, `python`, `yaml`, and `sql`, with their aliases.
A fence in any other language, or with none, renders as plain `pre.shiki` text with no token classes, and it never throws.
A fenced `mermaid` block passes through untouched and keeps `<code class="language-mermaid">` for a client-side diagram renderer.

The highlighter renders it as the following HTML:
Each rendered table is wrapped in `div.table-scroll` with `role="region"`, `tabindex="0"`, and an `aria-label` of `Table: ` plus the first header row's cell text, comma-joined.
When there is no header row, the label is `Table`.
The table stays a real table inside the wrapper.
Setting `tableScroll` to `false` turns the wrap off, as [Set the renderer options](#set-the-renderer-options) describes.
The following markdown is a two-column table:
The pipeline renders it as the following HTML:
The engine's `:::figure` directive keeps a placement class only when its `class` is exactly `center`, `wide`, or `full`, and it emits that class as `cairn-place-<role>`.
It ignores any other class without an error.
A figure with no `media:` image still renders as a `<figure>` around its other children.
The following directive is a `wide` figure with no image:
The pipeline renders it as the following HTML:
The engine writes these classes, and [Emitted classes](../reference/render.md#emitted-classes) lists each one with who styles it.
[Style rendered markdown](theme-your-public-site.md#style-rendered-markdown) covers styling them in the site's theme.
To turn off the table wrap or change the anchor `rel`, set the renderer options.
`createRenderer` takes a `RendererConfig` as its second argument, and its options extend the sanitize allowlist, set the table wrap and the anchor `rel`, and add a site's plugins.
In the adapter file, pass the options object as the second argument of the one `createRenderer` call.
The following table lists each option, its default, and what it does:
Option
Default
What it does
`sanitizeSchema`
cairn's default schema
Receives the default schema and returns the schema to use, to admit benign HTML the content needs
`tableScroll`
On
Wraps each table in `div.table-scroll`, and `false` turns the wrap off
`anchorRel`
`'noopener noreferrer'`
Sets the `rel` forced on every `target="_blank"` anchor, and `false` leaves the step out
`remarkPlugins`
None
Runs after cairn's remark steps and before the remark-to-rehype conversion
`rehypePlugins`
None
Runs last of all, after the table-scroll wrap
The remark steps a site's plugin follows are include resolution, the directive stamp, `cairn:` links, figures, and `media:` resolution.
The anchor step runs after highlighting and ahead of the sink guard, the table-scroll wrap, and the site's `rehypePlugins`.
It covers anchors that a component builds, but not an anchor that a site's `rehypePlugins` add.
No option turns highlighting off or changes it.
[The sanitize floor](../reference/render.md#the-sanitize-floor) states what a `sanitizeSchema` callback can't remove.
[Render safety](security-model.md#render-safety) sets out the pipeline's full stage order and what the sanitize floor protects.
Next, add a remark plugin.
A scaffolded site smartens quotes, dashes, and ellipses by passing `remark-smartypants` to its one `createRenderer` call through `remarkPlugins`.
Straight quotes, `--` and `---`, and `...` in body prose come out smartened the same way in the public render and the preview.
Inline code, code blocks, and link URLs stay untouched.
As a remark plugin, it runs over the markdown tree before the conversion to HTML.
The scaffold exports the plugin list from one module and passes it to `createRenderer` in the adapter:
On a scaffolded site, another remark plugin goes in the same `proseTypography` list.
To add the plugin to the tutorial's site, follow these steps:
In a terminal at the project root, install the plugin:
In `src/lib/cairn.config.ts`, pass the plugin to `createRenderer` through `remarkPlugins`:
The [remark-smartypants README](https://github.com/silvenon/remark-smartypants) lists the plugin's other options.
With the pipeline set, declare a custom public component.
`defineComponent` declares one container directive from a required `name`, `label`, `description`, and `build`, with `attributes`, `slots`, and `hydrate` optional.
The running example declares a `takeaways` component in `src/lib/markdown-components.ts`, a new module laid out like the scaffold's `markdown-components.ts`.
On a scaffolded site, declare it in the scaffold's `markdown-components.ts` beside the nine components already there.
To declare the component, follow these steps:
In the module, declare `takeaways` with its label, its description, and one attribute.
In the same module, export the component list:
The directive vocabulary is container-only.
An author opens a component with `:::name[Title]{attrs}` and closes it with `:::`.
A component with named slots takes a four-colon outer fence around its nested `:::slotName` containers.
A leaf `::name{attrs}` or text `:name{attrs}` form is restored to its literal source text.
The pipeline reads either form as a stray colon in prose, such as a time or a ratio.
`::include` is the one leaf form the pipeline reads, and [Reuse content across entries](reuse-content-across-entries.md) covers it.
The `attributes` member accepts exactly ten `fields.*` types, because each serializes to a single directive-attribute string.
The ten are `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `select`, `url`, `email`, `date`, `datetime`, `boolean`, and `icon`.
A `multiselect`, `object`, `array`, `reference`, or `image` attribute throws at declaration, and the message includes `a directive attribute must be a single-value scalar`.
The attributes are checked by the same fieldset machinery a concept's fields use.
`defineComponent` builds an `attributeSchema` with `defineFieldset(attributes, { behavior })`, and `validateComponent` runs it.
A cross-field rule therefore goes in the component's `behavior` table, keyed by attribute name.
The constructor sets `attributeSchema`, and a site never sets it.
The [`defineComponent`](../reference/core.md#definecomponent) entry lists the ten types and the `behavior` table.
The [Fields](../reference/core.md#fields) table states what each type renders and validates, including what an `icon` attribute needs from the adapter.
For `hydrate`, which opts the directive into a client island, see [Add an island](add-an-island.md).
Next, declare the regions an author fills.
A slot named `title` is the directive's bracketed label, a slot named `body` is its default content, and any other name is a named region.
The editor's insert dialog writes and reads `title` and `body` specially, as [Component authoring grammar](#component-authoring-grammar) shows.
The following table lists the members of a slot:
Member
What it does
`name` and `label`
Name the slot in the directive and label it in the insert form
`kind`
Takes `'inline'`, `'markdown'`, or `'repeatable'`
`required`
Marks the slot with an asterisk in the insert form and keeps **Insert** unavailable until it is filled, with one non-empty item for a repeatable slot.
Once the slot is touched, the form shows `<label> is required.`, and the insert validator repeats the check.
`itemFields`
For a repeatable slot, names each item's fields, but the insert form reads only the first declared field's key.
Each item is one string under that key, or under `text` when `itemFields` is absent.
`itemLabel`
For a repeatable slot, names each row in the insert form from that one-key record and the zero-based index.
When it returns nothing or blank text, the row reads as the slot label plus the row number.
The render pipeline never reads `required`, so a hand-typed directive without the slot still renders.
In the component's declaration, add a `slots` array with a required title, a markdown body, and a repeatable list of points:
The `points` slot declares no `itemFields`, so each item is one string under `text`, and its `itemLabel` names each row by that text.
Next, write the function that builds the component's markup.
`build` receives the directive's attributes and rendered slots and returns one hast `Element`, synchronously, once for each occurrence in the markdown.
The following table lists what the context passed to `build` carries:
Member
What it holds
`attributes`
The declared attribute values, keyed by attribute
`slot(name)`
A slot's rendered children, or an empty array when the slot is absent
`items(name)`
One list of children for each item of a repeatable slot
`attr(key)`
A declared attribute's string value, or `undefined` for a boolean or absent attribute
`node`
The stamped component element
The engine ships no hast-building helper beyond the context, so a site builds its markup with hastscript's `h()`.
The [Types](../reference/render.md#types) section documents `ComponentContext`.
In the component's declaration, replace the stub with a `build` that arranges the three slots inside an aside element:
`build` runs inline in the pipeline's tree transform and can't `await`.
Data a component needs is fetched outside the render pipeline and reaches `build` through the directive's attributes.
The engine stamps an entrance ordinal on the element `build` returns, and `build` adds no motion markup.
A component's inner classes need names apart from any DaisyUI component class, such as `card-body` or `card-title`.
DaisyUI's plugin generates CSS for a matching class name anywhere in scanned source.
A reused name is restyled when the site turns that DaisyUI component on elsewhere.
The example's `takeaways-*` classes follow the rule.
Next, shape how the component appears in the editor's picker.
The optional `icon`, `group`, `hidden`, `insertTemplate`, `use`, and `preview` members shape the component's row in the editor's picker.
The following table lists what each member does:
Member
What it does
`icon`
Names a glyph key from the site's icon set
`group`
Sets the heading the row sits under
`hidden`
Leaves the component out of the top-level picker
`insertTemplate`
Sets the markdown scaffold inserted at the cursor
`use`
Gives one line of guidance
`preview`
Supplies a sample, with optional `attributes` and `slots`, whose presence opts the configure step into the two-pane live preview
A non-empty `defaultIconByRole` map overrides the engine's role-to-glyph defaults.
In the component's declaration, add a `group`, a `use` line, and a `preview` sample:
With the component declared, register it.
`defineRegistry({ components })` builds the one registry that the render pipeline and the editor's component picker both read.
To register the component with the render pipeline, follow these steps:
In the adapter file, build the registry from the module's component list with `defineRegistry`.
On a scaffolded site, add `takeaways` to the `components` list in `markdown-components.ts` instead.
The scaffold's adapter already builds its registry from that list.
In the same file, pass `registry` as the first argument of `createRenderer`, in place of the empty registry.
In the adapter's `rendering` group, set `components: registry`, as the scaffold does.
`defineRegistry` throws for a component named `figure` or `include`, because the engine's render steps handle those directive names.
Its message says to remove the component if the built-in covers your use, or to rename it.
It also throws when a component sets a non-empty `defaultIconByRole` but declares no `type: 'icon'` attribute.
The [`defineRegistry`](../reference/core.md#defineregistry) entry documents the registry and its readers.
Before you verify, read the markdown an author writes for the component.
Checking the component in the editor means reading the markdown the insert dialog writes: a four-colon outer fence holding one nested `:::slotName` container for each named slot.
An author writes the `takeaways` directive like this:
The registered `build` turns it into this HTML:
A repeatable slot's items are bullet lines inside its container.
The `title` slot is the bracketed label, and the `body` slot is the default content.
A directive's bracketed label is dropped when the component declares no `title` slot.
With the grammar in hand, check the component end to end.
The component renders the same markup in the edit page's preview and on the published page.
To verify the render, follow these steps:
In a terminal, start the site's dev server.
In the admin, open an entry.
In the editor, insert the component from the picker, under its `group`.
In the editor, check that the inserted markdown has the four-colon fence and the nested slot container.
In the editor's preview, check that the component's markup appears after a short pause and updates as you type.
With the plugin from [Add a remark plugin](#add-a-remark-plugin) in place, a straight quote typed in body prose shows curly.
In the admin, publish the entry.
On the entry's public page, after the deploy, check that the component element's classes match the preview's.
When a check fails, [Diagnose a failed check](#diagnose-a-failed-check) lists the causes in the order of these steps.
Each failed check traces to a declaration or to the markdown an author wrote, and the causes follow the order of the verification steps:
The dev server stops at startup with an error that names the component.
An attribute of a type outside the ten throws `a directive attribute must be a single-value scalar ...`.
A component named `figure` or `include` throws with the remove-or-rename message.
A `defaultIconByRole` with no `type: 'icon'` attribute throws as well.
Correct the declaration as [Declare a component](#declare-a-component) and [Register the component](#register-the-component) describe.
The component is missing from the picker.
A component whose declaration sets `hidden` is left out of the top-level picker, as [Shape the picker entry](#shape-the-picker-entry) states.
The directive shows as literal text in the preview.
It was written in the leaf `::name` or text `:name` form, which always restores to its source text.
Rewrite it as a container directive.
A code block shows no token colors in the preview or on the page.
Its fence names a language outside the preloaded set, and such a fence renders as plain `pre.shiki` text.
The preloaded languages are listed in [Built-in render steps](#built-in-render-steps).
For any other failure, read the running site's output in [Read the structured logs](debug-your-site.md#read-the-structured-logs).

[`createRenderer`](../reference/core.md#createrenderer): the renderer and its options.
[`defineComponent`](../reference/core.md#definecomponent) and [`defineRegistry`](../reference/core.md#defineregistry): the component and registry entries.
[Render authoring](../reference/render.md): `ComponentContext` and the emitted classes.
[Render safety](security-model.md#render-safety): what the sanitize floor and the sink guard protect.
[Add an island](add-an-island.md): hydrating a component in the browser.
[Style rendered markdown](theme-your-public-site.md#style-rendered-markdown): styling the rendered output.
[Reuse content across entries](reuse-content-across-entries.md): fragments and `::include`.
[Configure media](configure-media.md): the media resolver that `render` forwards, and what a missing asset renders.
